title: Smart windowed sampler for console ingest to reduce hot-key amplification
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: A small number of hot keys from certain tenants cause downstream stream processors and enrichment workers to spike CPU, evict KV cache entries, and trigger tenant-level pre-scaling. Existing admission controls blunt spikes but either increase tail latency for all tenants (global queueing) or drop important signal (coarse drops).

Goal: Implement a Smart Windowed Sampler (SWS) — a compact, per-tenant lossy buffer + time-windowed sampling policy that preserves representative metric samples while limiting amplification to downstream processors. The SWS should: (1) reduce downstream CPU and IO for pathological hot-key patterns, (2) keep percentiles and aggregate counts within defined error bounds, and (3) be safe to enable in a canary region and roll back quickly.

High-level approach: Maintain a fixed-size ring-reservoir per tenant keyed by (route, metric-type, short-key-hash). Each ring stores lightweight summaries (timestamp, compact payload pointer, weight). Samples are admitted deterministically via a windowed rate-limiter + reservoir replacement policy that prefers newer events but keeps sparse historical representation for percentile stability. An optional mini-eviction pass serializes accepted samples into compressed micro-batches for downstream consumers.

Why different from prior work: Instead of global sampling or pure LRU drops, SWS biases for temporal recency within short windows (100ms-5s) but retains long-tail representative samples using weighted reservoir sampling. This keeps tail-shape information for quality and alerting while bounding worst-case ingestion amplification.

Safety: circuit-breaker flags per-tenant, per-route; sampling policy feature-flagged; observability hooks emitting admitted_vs_seen, sample_weight_hist, and eviction_rate.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end canary in us-west-2 without increased error rate for console-ingest customers
Downstream enrichment CPU reduced >= 15% for synthetic hotkey workload (50x frequency skew)
p95/p99 of console ingestion end-to-end (ingress -> enrichment commit) does not regress by more than 5% for normal traffic profile
Sampling error: aggregated count drift < 3% and metric percentile drift within defined SLA for synthetic workloads
Feature flag + emergency disable that fully bypasses SWS in <30s via control plane toggle
steps: Design RFC and microbench (prototype library in go/proto) — include deterministic hashing and memory budget model
Local simulation harness using historic console traces to tune window sizes and reservoir sizes
Implement minimal hot-path C++/Go path with fast admit and minimal allocation (thin pointer to compressed payload store)
Add observability metrics and debug logs; wire into Console-Observability dashboard (per-tenant admitted_vs_seen, sample_weight_hist)
Run cluster-level load tests and synthetic hotkey scenarios; capture regression and stability metrics
Canary deployment to us-west-2 for 48 hours with progressive traffic ramp and rollback plan
Post-canary review, follow-up performance tuning, and rollout to additional regions
